title: ESP32-S3-WROOM PCB antenna keepout — Hub Standard
rule: A 21mm x 48mm keepout zone (all 4 layers: no tracks, vias, pads, copper pours, or footprints) must be present over the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 PCB-trace antenna lobe on the Hub Standard board. The zone corresponds to the region extending past the module edge opposite the pads, as defined by the WROOM datasheet keepout polygon.
rationale: The ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 uses a PCB trace antenna for 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. Any copper or components under the antenna degrade radiation pattern and efficiency. The Hub Standard explicitly honors this keepout for future Wi-Fi (spec §4, CLAUDE.md). Violating it on any layer silently degrades the radio.
scope: Hub Standard board only (hubs/hub-standard). Identify by: footprint contains 'WROOM' or 'S3-WROOM'. The keepout zone must span all copper layers (F.Cu, In1.Cu, In2.Cu, B.Cu) on the antenna lobe side of the module. Not applicable to MINI-1 or C6-MINI-1 modules (modules do not use the WROOM; wired-only modules dropped the antenna keepout). (merged dup)
check_method: Parse hub-standard.kicad_pcb for a rule-area zone of type keepout with tracks_not_allowed + vias_not_allowed + copperpour_not_allowed + pads_not_allowed + footprints_not_allowed. Verify zone polygon encompasses the WROOM antenna lobe region (approximately (50,104)-(71,152) in the current board). Also verify no footprint courtyard or copper overlaps the zone.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline PLACEMENT stage (chk_on_board via DRC); zone itself must be present as a pre-condition
source: CLAUDE.md §Hub Standard table: 'ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM; PCB-antenna keepout honored for future Wi-Fi)'; hub-standard.kicad_pcb keepout zone at lines ~1100-1140; cec_pcb.py courtyard_bbox drop_keepout logic

title: ESP32-C6/S3-MINI antenna keepout — wired-only modules may drop it
rule: On modules confirmed wired-only (no Wi-Fi at runtime), the ESP32-MINI antenna lobe keepout MAY be dropped (drop_keepout=True) to reclaim board area. On any module where Wi-Fi is populated or possible, the full MINI keepout must be respected. The drop_keepout flag must be an explicit design decision recorded in the board's generator or build config.
rationale: The ESP32-C6-MINI-1 (24-pin, EPS, PCIe digital-sensor modules) and ESP32-S3-MINI-1 (12VHPWR Standard) are wired-only — no Wi-Fi in use. Dropping the ~12x22mm keepout lobe recovers significant area on small boards. cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox implements this as drop_keepout=True. Keeping the keepout on a wired-only module wastes area needlessly; accidentally dropping it on a Wi-Fi-enabled module breaks the radio.
scope: All modules with ESP32-MINI footprints (modules/eps-8pin, modules/atx-24pin, modules/pcie-8pin-2port, modules/pcie-8pin-3port, modules/12vhpwr-standard). Identify by: footprint libid contains 'ESP32-C6-MINI' or 'ESP32-S3-MINI'. Check params.respect_antenna_keepout in cec_synth_pipeline Config.
check_method: In cec_synth_pipeline.py, extract_features() derives 'wireless': bool(cfg.params.get('respect_antenna_keepout', True)). Verify that wired-only modules have respect_antenna_keepout=False in their config and that the board's keepout zone (if present) matches the intended keepout state. For a board claiming wired-only, verify no Wi-Fi-dependent BOM line is present.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline EMC analysis arm (_emc_applies checks 'wireless'); cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox drop_keepout parameter
source: CLAUDE.md §Done history: 'ESP32-C6 antenna keepout DROPPED (no wireless, per user) -> GND fills under it'; cec_pcb.py lines 87-130 courtyard_bbox/drop_keepout; cec_synth_pipeline.py extract_features() 'wireless' key

title: USB D+/D− differential pair — hard routing gate
rule: USB_D_P and USB_D_N (the module debug USB pair, and the Hub Standard native USB pair) must both be fully routed with zero unconnected ratlines. This is a HARD GATE: any candidate where either net has an unrouted stub fails outright. The pair must use the _P/_N naming convention for KiCad auto-recognition.
rationale: USB Full Speed (12 Mbps) requires a matched differential pair. An unrouted D+ or D− breaks USB enumeration entirely — the board cannot be programmed or used. The cec_score diffpair_ok gate enforces this as a pipeline hard gate identical in severity to the Kelvin sense gate.
scope: All boards with USB (all modules for debug USB-C J5, Hub Standard for host USB). Identify nets by: name ends in '_P' and has a matching '_N' counterpart. Specifically: /USB_D_P and /USB_D_N (after the v2026-06-06 rename from /USB_DP and /USB_DM on EPS; Hub Standard still uses the legacy names on the PCB).
check_method: cec_score._derive_pairs() finds all *_P/*_N pairs. Metrics.diffpair_ok = True iff every diff pair has >= 1 routed track segment AND 0 unconnected ratlines on both members. Run via cec_score.score() -> gate(). Also verify net names: any board with /USB_DP or /USB_DM (old names) should be flagged for rename to _P/_N.
source: cec_score.py lines 50-68 _derive_pairs, line 124 diffpair_ok HARD GATE; CLAUDE.md: 'USB is now an AUTO-RECOGNIZED diff pair -- renamed /USB_DP->/USB_D_P, /USB_DM->/USB_D_N'

title: USB D+/D− diff pair routing impedance window (DRU)
rule: The USB diff pair gap must be 0.10–0.20mm (EPS/PCIe/modules DRU) or 0.12–0.20mm (Hub Standard DRU). Track width must be 0.15–0.25mm on the Hub Standard board. The pair must be routed together over a continuous GND reference plane with no splits or voids directly beneath the pair.
rationale: USB Full Speed is impedance-tolerant (~90Ω ±15%), but a grossly wrong gap or width breaks coupling and causes reflections. The DRU gap constraint enforces coupled routing. USB High Speed (Hub Pro) requires tight 90Ω ±5% — the hub-standard DRU comment explicitly notes FS is tolerant but HS is not, and the Hub Pro must be tightened when specified.
scope: All boards with USB netclass (identified by nets matching /USB_D_P, /USB_D_N). DRU rule: condition 'A.NetClass == "USB" && B.NetClass == "USB"' for gap, 'A.NetClass == "USB"' for width. Hub Standard: gap min 0.12mm max 0.20mm, width min 0.15mm max 0.25mm. Modules: gap min 0.10mm max 0.20mm.
check_method: Verify .kicad_dru contains the USB diff_pair_gap rule. Run kicad-cli pcb drc and check for diff_pair_gap and track_width violations on USB netclass nets. Verify the pair routes over In1.Cu (GND plane) with no plane splits directly beneath.
existing_checker: hub-standard.kicad_dru 'USB diff pair gap' and 'USB diff pair width' rules; eps8pin-module.kicad_dru 'USB diff pair gap'; 24pin-module.kicad_dru 'USB diff pair gap'
source: hubs/hub-standard/hub-standard.kicad_dru lines 42-47; modules/eps-8pin/eps8pin-module.kicad_dru lines 16-18; modules/atx-24pin/24pin-module.kicad_dru lines 38-40; CLAUDE.md: 'USB diff pair gap0.13 /USB_D_P,/USB_D_N'

title: CAN_H/CAN_L tightly coupled routing (non-P/N asymmetric names)
rule: CAN_H and CAN_L must be routed as a tightly coupled differential pair on the same layer over a continuous GND reference plane. Because they use asymmetric industry-standard names (not _P/_N), KiCad's auto-diff-pair router does NOT recognize them automatically — they must be routed manually as a coupled pair. Maximum uncoupled stub length: keep stubs to the transceiver (U2 TJA1051T/3) as short as possible, ideally under 5mm.
rationale: Classical CAN at 500kbps is forgiving, but the optional 1Mbps rate (spec §3.1 v3.4) places the bus in the star/stub topology where ringing on uncoupled stubs gates the 1Mbps option. The TJA1051T/3 is NOT a SIC part, so no transceiver-side ringing suppression is available — the passive topology result depends entirely on the PCB coupling and stub geometry. Short coupled stubs to the transceiver are the design defense.
scope: All boards with CAN transceiver (all boards). Identify nets: /CAN_H, /CAN_L (or /CAN1_H, /CAN1_L). Identify transceiver: ref starting with U and value containing 'TJA1051'. Hub Standard: 4 ports each with a short stub from the split termination R3/R4/C7 to J2-J5 pins 3/6.
check_method: Verify CAN_H and CAN_L nets are in the CAN netclass (check .kicad_pro net_settings). Verify the DRU has no CAN-specific rule (by design — standard diff is adequate per hub-standard.kicad_dru comment). Verify visually/geometrically that CAN_H and CAN_L route in parallel within ~0.2mm gap on the same layer. Check that U2 (TJA1051T/3) is placed close to its RJ-45 port(s).
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline CONFORMANCE chk_can_present (verifies CAN nets exist)
source: hubs/hub-standard/hub-standard.kicad_dru lines 49-52: 'No CAN-specific rule... Keep CAN_H/CAN_L coupled and short'; eps8pin-module.kicad_dru: 'CAN_H/CAN_L keep the standard (asymmetric) names -> NOT a P/N auto-pair; route them as a tightly-coupled pair by hand'; spec §3.1

title: CAN termination 120Ω split at Hub only — never on modules
rule: The fixed 120Ω split termination (two 60Ω resistors + 4.7nF cap) must be present at the Hub and absent on every module. No module may carry CAN termination resistors on the CAN_H/CAN_L bus nets.
rationale: CAN requires exactly one 120Ω termination per stub endpoint on a star topology. The Hub is one endpoint; the other end is terminated by the cable impedance and the spec-defined Hub-only split. A module adding its own termination creates a parallel path that drops the effective termination below 60Ω, causing dominant-bit timing errors and protocol failures. This is a locked platform decision (spec §3.1).
scope: All modules (identify: board is in modules/ directory, not hubs/). On modules: verify no resistors with values 60Ω, 120Ω, or 0.12k are connected between CAN_H and CAN_L. On Hub: verify R3 and R4 (60Ω each) with C7 (4.7nF) form the split termination.
check_method: cec_synth_pipeline CONFORMANCE chk_no_module_can_term: parse netlist for module boards, find any R between CAN_H and CAN_L nets, flag if value is 60Ω or 120Ω. On Hub boards: verify the split termination components exist with correct values.
source: spec §3.1: 'Termination: fixed 120 ohm split at Hub'; CLAUDE.md: 'No module CAN termination (Hub-only)'; cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage chk_no_module_can_term

title: CAN star topology — stub length equalization at Hub
rule: On the Hub, each RJ-45 port's CAN_H/CAN_L stub from the split termination network to the port jack should be kept as equal in length as practical. Maximum stub imbalance advisory: <10mm difference between longest and shortest port stub.
rationale: A star topology with unequal stubs presents different propagation delays per port. At 500kbps this is negligible, but at the optional 1Mbps rate with no SIC transceiver ringing suppression, unequal stubs create asymmetric reflections that can degrade the eye. Equalizing stubs is the cheapest SI improvement available.
scope: Hub boards only (hubs/hub-standard, hubs/hub-pro). Identify CAN_H and CAN_L nets connecting to multiple RJ-45 jacks (J2-J5 on Hub Standard).
check_method: Measure routed length of CAN_H and CAN_L from the R3/R4 split termination to each port jack pad. Compute max-min delta. Flag if delta > 10mm. Requires routed board.
source: spec §3.1: 'star topology with up to 8 stubs must be signal-integrity verified'; hub-standard.kicad_dru comment: 'on-board it is a short multidrop stub bus to the 4 ports'

title: FTP shielded RJ-45 SH1/SH2 pads tied to GND
rule: On every board carrying the FTP shielded RJ-45 (cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal, Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C / LCSC C2683360), both shield tab pads SH1 and SH2 must be connected to GND. This applies to: Hub Standard (J2-J5), 12VHPWR Standard (J1), and EPS 8-pin (J1). No unconnected shield tab pads on FTP jacks.
rationale: Both-end shield grounding is the spec-locked configuration (CLAUDE.md v2026-06-06: 'both-end shielding+grounding, per the user'). An unconnected shield tab is an EMC failure mode — the cable shield becomes a floating conductor that can re-radiate instead of absorbing. The M3 chassis bond at both Hub and module provides the ground loop path; at intra-case RJ-45 lengths the ground loop impedance is negligible.
scope: All boards with footprint cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal. Identify by: footprint libid contains 'RJ45_FTP_Shielded'. Check pad names SH1 and SH2. Currently applies to: hubs/hub-standard J2-J5, modules/eps-8pin J1, modules/12vhpwr-standard J1. The 24-pin and PCIe boards still use unshielded 54602 — shield constraint does NOT apply to them yet.
check_method: Parse netlist: for each component with footprint containing 'RJ45_FTP', find pads named SH1 and SH2. Verify both are assigned to GND net (net name is 'GND' or ends in '/GND'). A no-connect flag on SH1 or SH2 of an FTP jack is a violation.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'gen-modules.py now EMITS the FTP footprint + SH1/SH2->GND'; 'SH1/SH2 -> GND (both-end shielding+grounding, per the user)'; modules/eps-8pin/eps8pin-module.kicad_dru header comment; modules/12vhpwr-standard schematic note

title: RJ-45 pin allocation matches locked table
rule: Every RJ-45 connector J1 (modules) or J2-J5 (Hub) must have: pin 1 = +5VSB/VCC, pin 2 = GND, pin 3 = CAN_H or CAN1_H, pin 6 = CAN_L or CAN1_L, pin 8 = DETECT. Pin 7 must be reserved spare — NOT connected to any reference, analog, or auxiliary net (not AUX_REF, not REF, not any net containing REF).
rationale: The pin allocation is the locked universal interface (spec §2.2). Wrong pin assignment on a shipping board causes CAN bus faults, DETECT misread, or power cross-connection across every installed module. This is irreversible without a PCB spin.
scope: All boards. Identify RJ-45 components by footprint containing 'RJ45' or 'RJ-45' or value '8P8C'. Check all 8 data pads plus pin 7.
check_method: cec_synth_pipeline CONFORMANCE chk_pin_allocation: for the RJ-45 component, call nl.net_of(ref, pin) for pins 1,2,3,6,7,8. Verify pin 1 net contains 'VCC' or '5VSB'; pin 2 net contains 'GND'; pin 3 net contains 'CAN'; pin 6 net contains 'CAN'; pin 8 net contains 'DETECT'; pin 7 net does NOT contain 'AUX' or 'REF'. Flag any mismatch.
source: spec §2.2 pin allocation table; CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'Pinout on every board matches the locked pin allocation table (pin 7 is a reserved spare, NOT AUX_REF)'; cec_synth_pipeline.py chk_pin_allocation

title: DETECT pin 8 ESD protection diode on every board
rule: Every Hub port and every module must carry a low-capacitance ESD diode on the DETECT pin 8 line. The correct part is PESD5V0S1BA (SOD-323, LCSC C5261083) — cathode to the DETECT line, anode to GND. PESD5V0S1UL is the wrong package designation (DFN1006/SOD-882 in LCSC stock) — do not use it.
rationale: DETECT feeds the ESP32 ADC directly with no inherent input protection. The platform hot-plugs modules, so insertion ESD lands on a bare analog input. A single low-capacitance ESD diode is a locked platform-wide requirement (spec §2.4 v2.0). Low capacitance (<1pF) is required to not load the 10kΩ/3.3V divider. Locked part: PESD5V0S1BA SOD-323.
scope: Hub Standard: D2-D5 one per port (cathode to each /DETECT_Pn net, anode to GND). All modules: D1 on the DETECT net. Identify the DETECT net by: connected to RJ-45 pin 8, contains 'DETECT' in net name. Identify the ESD diode by: ref D1 (modules) or D2-D5 (hub), SOD-323 footprint, PESD5V0S1BA value. Board state: Hub Standard D2-D5 done; modules carry D1 in the schematic, footprint assigned at layout; ordered 24-pin rev2 shipped without it (rev3 picks it up). (merged dup)
check_method: For each DETECT net: verify exactly one ESD diode component (value = PESD5V0S1BA, footprint = SOD-323) is present with cathode on the DETECT net and anode on GND. Flag if missing, if wrong part value (PESD5V0S1UL), or if wrong polarity. Hub Standard D2-D5 verified as DONE. EPS/PCIe modules: D1 present but footprint not yet assigned (flag as warning). 24-pin rev2: absent (known gap, flag).
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline CONFORMANCE (no dedicated check yet — new checker needed); CLAUDE.md action item 1
source: spec §2.4: 'A single low-capacitance ESD diode on pin 8 is locked into every Hub and module (decision, v2.0)'; CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'D1 = PESD5V0S1BA (SOD-323, LCSC C5261083)'; CLAUDE.md action item 1

title: DETECT code resistor value matches §2.3 table
rule: The DETECT resistor (R1 on modules, the per-port pull-down on Hub) must match the §2.3 code table for the module's comm-class: CAN-only modules (24-pin, EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR Standard) = 2.2kΩ (E24, ±1% tolerance acceptable). 12VHPWR Pro = 4.7kΩ. Resistor must be from pin 8 to GND (not pull-up). This is a standard 1% 0402 — no TCR or precision requirement.
rationale: The Hub reads DETECT through a fixed 10kΩ pull-up to 3.3V to determine which link to bring up. A wrong resistor value causes the Hub to misconfigure its port (e.g. attempting RS-485 on a CAN-only module, or vice versa). Codes are spaced ~0.45V apart — a wrong value by even one E24 step may fall in a different code bin.
scope: All modules. Identify: R1 on the DETECT net (net name contains 'DETECT'). Board profile determines expected value: Standard modules = 2.2kΩ; Pro modules = 4.7kΩ. Read from cfg.params['detect_ohms'] in synth pipeline.
check_method: cec_synth_pipeline CONFORMANCE chk_detect_resistor: find resistors on the DETECT net, parse their value to ohms via _r_value_ohms(), check abs(val - expected) / expected < 0.10. Flag if no resistor found or value is wrong. Also verify resistor connects DETECT to GND (not to a power rail).
source: spec §2.3 DETECT code table; CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'CAN-only 2.2 kΩ (24-pin/EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR-Std), 12VHPWR Pro = 4.7 kΩ'; cec_synth_pipeline.py chk_detect_resistor

title: RS-485 streaming pair (pins 4/5) absent on Standard modules and Hubs
rule: Standard-tier modules must NOT populate RS-485 receivers or transmitters on pair 2 (pins 4/5 = STREAM_P/STREAM_N). The STREAM_P/STREAM_N nets on Standard boards must be absent or terminated only with a passive pull-down/stub at the module side. Pro+ boards must populate the RS-485 driver/receiver.
rationale: RS-485 is a tier-differentiating feature (spec §3.2). Populating streaming hardware on a Standard module inflates BOM cost without function (the Standard Hub has no RS-485 receiver). An RS-485 driver on a Standard module would drive the pair unexpectedly if misconfigured, potentially interfering with Pro module streaming on a mixed hub.
scope: All modules. Identify Standard modules by: MCU is ESP32-C6-MINI or ESP32-S3-MINI (not P4). Check for any RS-485 transceiver component (value contains '485' or 'MAX485' or 'SP485'). Identify Pro modules by: MCU is ESP32-P4 — verify RS-485 transceiver is present.
check_method: cec_synth_pipeline CONFORMANCE chk_rs485_tiering: check if STREAM_P/STREAM_N nets exist and are connected to an RS-485 transceiver component. On Standard modules (MCU != P4): flag any RS-485 transceiver present. On Pro modules (MCU = P4): flag if RS-485 transceiver is absent.
source: spec §3.2: 'Present on Pro modules and Pro+ Hubs. Standard does not populate it'; CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'RS-485 pair (pins 4 and 5)... present only on Pro and above'; cec_synth_pipeline.py chk_rs485_tiering

title: Continuous GND plane under signal routing (In1.Cu/L2)
rule: CAN_H/CAN_L and USB_D+/D− must route over a continuous solid GND pour on In1.Cu (L2). Anti-pad voids from high-current via arrays in the GND plane must not interrupt the return path directly beneath any of these signal nets. Acceptable: anti-pads displaced laterally from the signal trace with at least one solid GND copper width between the void edge and the trace.
rationale: Return current travels in the GND plane directly beneath differential signal traces. A void in the GND plane under a differential pair forces return current to detour, increasing loop inductance, causing a reference-plane discontinuity, and increasing EMI. High-current via arrays on EPS/PCIe boards punch anti-pad voids in L2 — spec §6.7 explicitly calls out 'keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids'.
scope: All boards. Identify signal nets requiring continuous GND: /CAN_H, /CAN_L, /USB_D_P, /USB_D_N, /STREAM_P, /STREAM_N. Identify high-current via arrays: clusters of vias on nets containing '12V' or '/SENSEC'. Check that routing of CAN/USB traces on L1 or L4 does not cross over GND plane voids from those via arrays.
check_method: Partial: parse board for ZONE fill polygons on In1.Cu (GND net). Parse via array positions on high-current nets. Verify no differential signal trace segment on any layer passes within its own width of a GND plane anti-pad void. Full check requires geometric intersection analysis of trace bounding boxes vs. zone cutouts.
source: spec §6.7: 'Via arrays punch anti-pad voids in the L2 ground pour; keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids'; hub-standard.kicad_dru comment: 'CAN_H/L and USB_D+/- are 100% on F.Cu over In1 with 0 vias (good)'; CLAUDE.md action item 3(a)

title: Signal net board-edge clearance — slot-antenna prevention
rule: CAN_H, CAN_L, USB_D_P, USB_D_N, STREAM_P, STREAM_N, and DETECT traces must maintain at least 0.5mm clearance from Edge.Cuts. Traces within 0.2mm of the board edge are at risk of acting as slot antennas, radiating EMI proportional to signal edge rate.
rationale: A trace parallel to and close to a board edge forms a slot antenna at frequencies where the trace length approaches λ/4. CAN at 500kbps–1Mbps has harmonic content up to ~5MHz where even short edge segments can couple. The Hub Standard PCB review (CLAUDE.md action 3c) specifically flagged CAN_RX/CAN_L traces at 0.03–0.13mm from the board edge as a slot-antenna risk.
scope: All boards. Identify affected nets: /CAN_H, /CAN_L, /USB_D_P, /USB_D_N, /STREAM_P, /STREAM_N, /DETECT. Measure minimum distance from any track segment on these nets to the nearest Edge.Cuts line.
check_method: Run kicad-cli pcb drc and check copper_edge_clearance violations on the named nets. Alternatively, parse board for track segments on these nets and compute minimum distance to Edge.Cuts polygons. Flag any segment within 0.5mm. CLAUDE.md cites 0.03–0.13mm as the current Hub Standard failure case.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline PLACEMENT chk_on_board (partial: catches copper_edge_clearance DRC violations)
source: CLAUDE.md action item 3: 'Pull CAN_RX/CAN_L in from the board edge (~0.03-0.13mm now -> slot-antenna)'; hub-standard PCB DRC note; spec §3.1 board-edge routing guidance

title: Power netclass trace width ≥ 0.5mm (DRU safety net)
rule: Any track segment assigned to the Power netclass (nets +3V3, +5VSB, +5V_HOLD, USB_VBUS) must be at least 0.5mm wide. The 5VSB trunk (J1 power-in → mux → distribution star) must be poured or routed ≥1.5mm at 1oz. This is a DRU-enforced floor, not the primary sizing mechanism — trunk sizing is verified by IPC-2152 copper area.
rationale: The .kicad_dru Power min-width rule is a safety net against accidental hairlines on power distribution. Without it a default 0.2mm track on +5VSB passes DRC silently while being a thermal and reliability risk. The Hub Standard PCB review found 38 track_width DRC errors after the netclass-pattern fix (CLAUDE.md action 3b) — these are real faults, not false positives.
scope: All boards. Identify Power netclass nets from .kicad_pro: patterns /+3V3, /+5VSB, /+5V_HOLD, /USB_VBUS (with leading slash). The trunk net (/5VSB_RAW on Hub Standard) requires ≥1.5mm or pour.
check_method: Run kicad-cli pcb drc with the board's .kicad_dru active. Check for track_width violations on Power netclass nets. Separately identify the trunk trace (from power-in J1 to mux U5) and verify its width or pour copper area meets IPC-2152 for 3A at the board's copper weight.
existing_checker: hub-standard.kicad_dru 'Power min width' rule; eps8pin-module.kicad_dru; 24pin-module.kicad_dru; cec_synth_pipeline DFM chk_dfm_drc (track_width type)
source: hubs/hub-standard/hub-standard.kicad_dru lines 27-29; CLAUDE.md action 3(b): 'DRC now reports 38 track_width errors on the power nets'; spec §2.5 trunk sizing

title: Kelvin sense pairs (_HI/_LO) — hard routing gate on connectivity
rule: Every Kelvin sense pair (*_HI and *_LO) must be fully routed with zero unconnected ratlines on both members. This is a HARD GATE: any candidate where either *_HI or *_LO has an unrouted ratline fails outright, regardless of DRC count.
rationale: An unrouted Kelvin tap means the INA sense input is floating — the current measurement is completely wrong or absent. This is a measurement correctness requirement, not a performance optimization. The cec_score.kelvin_ok gate was specifically added to prevent a route from appearing 'mostly done' while the most critical measurement net is disconnected.
scope: All boards with shunts (EPS, PCIe, 24-pin, 12VHPWR). Identify Kelvin pairs by: net name ends in '_HI' and has a counterpart ending in '_LO' with the same stem. E.g. /SENSEC1_HI + /SENSEC1_LO, /IN1_P + /IN1_N (for INA240 filtered inputs). Stems: /SENSEC1, /SENSEC2 on EPS; /SENSEC1-3 on PCIe.
check_method: cec_score._derive_pairs() identifies all *_HI/*_LO pairs. Metrics.kelvin_ok = True iff every pair has >=1 routed track segment AND 0 unconnected ratlines on both members. Run via cec_score.score() -> gate(). Also check cec_synth_pipeline ROUTE_GATE chk_kelvin_gate.
existing_checker: cec_score.Metrics.kelvin_ok (HARD GATE); cec_synth_pipeline ROUTE_GATE chk_kelvin_gate; cec_synth_pipeline MEASURE chk_kelvin_topology
source: cec_score.py lines 50-51 _RE_KELVIN_HI, lines 54-68 _derive_pairs, line 123 kelvin_ok HARD GATE; spec §6.8: 'Four-wire Kelvin sensing on every shunt'

title: Kelvin sense taps on L1 (F.Cu), short, no vias
rule: Kelvin sense taps (*_HI/*_LO from the shunt inner sense pads to the INA input pins) must be routed on L1 (F.Cu) only, must be ≤3mm total length per tap, and must not use any vias. The taps must connect to the shunt's INNER sense terminals (not the force terminals).
rationale: Via inductance and trace length on the Kelvin tap add series impedance that appears in the measurement loop and degrades current accuracy. Spec §6.8 (LOCKED): 'Keep the Kelvin sense pair short and local on the top layer next to the shunt and its monitor. Do not route it down to a signal layer and back, which folds via inductance and trace length into the measurement.' At 0.5mΩ shunt values, even 1Ω trace inductance at AC frequencies matters for transient detection accuracy.
scope: All boards with shunts. Identify Kelvin taps: track segments on *_HI and *_LO nets. Identify shunt placement: RS* components. Check that the tap originates at the shunt inner sense pad (not force pad) and terminates at the INA U* sense input, staying on F.Cu, with no via in between.
check_method: Parse board for tracks on *_HI and *_LO nets. Verify: (1) all track segments are on layer F.Cu (not B.Cu, In1.Cu, In2.Cu); (2) total routed length from shunt pad to INA pad is ≤3mm; (3) no via is present on these nets between the shunt and the INA. NOTE: cec_score.kelvin_ok only checks connectivity — this additional layer/via/length check requires new code. The cec_synth_pipeline MEASURE chk_kelvin_topology checks topology (shunt straddles pair + INA present) but not layer/length.
source: spec §6.8 (LOCKED): 'Keep the Kelvin sense pair short and local on the top layer next to the shunt and its monitor. Do not route it down to a signal layer and back'; CLAUDE.md action -2: 'sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)'; CLAUDE.md stackup: 'L1: sensors and components, including the shunts'

title: INA sense IC must be physically adjacent to its shunt
rule: Each INA238/INA228/INA240/INA181 current-sense IC must be placed immediately adjacent to the shunt it senses (≤3mm between closest IC pad and closest shunt pad). The sense IC must be on the same side of the board as the shunt (both on F.Cu). No other component may be placed between the shunt sense pads and the INA sense input pads.
rationale: The Kelvin sense path length constraint (≤3mm, no vias, L1 only) cannot be satisfied unless the INA is physically adjacent to the shunt. Placement further away forces longer Kelvin traces that violate spec §6.8. CLAUDE.md action item -2 explicitly lists 'sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)' as deferred work that must be added as a hard constraint when the synth placer resumes.
scope: All boards with shunts and INA sense ICs. Identify shunt-to-INA mapping: each cable has one RS* shunt + one U* INA (INA238 for EPS/PCIe, INA228 for 24-pin, INA240 for 12VHPWR, INA181 for §6.13 detection). The INA ref can be derived from netlist: INA inputs IN+ and IN- connect to *_HI and *_LO which connect to the shunt inner pads.
check_method: For each (shunt RS_n, INA U_n) pair identified from netlist: compute Euclidean distance between the INA's closest sense-input pad centroid and the shunt's closest inner sense pad centroid in the placed board. Flag if distance > 3mm or if the INA is on a different board side than the shunt.
source: spec §6.8 (LOCKED); CLAUDE.md action -2: 'adding these as HARD constraints is a LOT more work or an entire reconsideration of the placement approach. WHEN RESUMED, the design pass must add: (2) sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)'

title: INA240 input RC filter: matched 10Ω Rf + 470nF differential cap per channel
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard module, each INA240 input pair must have matched 10Ω series resistors (RFH_n and RFL_n, 0.1%/50ppm, Yageo RT0402BRE07-10RL or equivalent) on both IN+ and IN− inputs, plus a 470nF differential capacitor (CF_n) across the filtered inputs. fc = 1/(2π × 2×Rf × Cdiff) ≈ 16.9kHz. Both Rf resistors in a pair must use the same value (matched within 0.1%) for CMRR preservation.
rationale: Mismatched Rf resistors degrade the INA240's common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) at the filter pole. At the ~10kHz GPU transient frequency of interest, even 1Ω mismatch in the 10Ω Rf pair introduces ~40dB CMRR degradation. Spec explicitly: 'matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470 nF differential cap (CF1-6)' and 'Rf held at 10 ohm + matched (TI's INA240 ceiling) for negligible gain/CMRR error'.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module only (modules/12vhpwr-standard). Identify: RFH1-6 and RFL1-6 (10Ω 0.1%) + CF1-6 (470nF). Check BOM: both RFH and RFL must be the same MPN (C705642 Yageo RT0402BRE07-10RL or equivalent 0.1% 50ppm 0402).
check_method: Parse BOM for refs RFH1-6 and RFL1-6: verify all 12 have identical value (10Ω), tolerance (0.1%), and MPN. Parse for CF1-6: verify value is 470nF. Check netlist: RFH_n connects between SENSEC_n_HI and IN_n_P; RFL_n connects between SENSEC_n_LO and IN_n_N; CF_n connects between IN_n_P and IN_n_N.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470 nF differential cap (CF1-6), fc = 1/(2*pi*2*Rf*Cdiff) ~= 16.9 kHz'; spec §6.1 12VHPWR Standard sensing; CLAUDE.md: 'RFH/RFL filter 10ohm DONE 2026-06-06 -> 0.1% Yageo RT0402BRE0710RL (C705642)'

title: VRAIL_DIV ADC input: 1nF C0G cap at R6 junction
rule: The VRAIL_DIV node (output of the 47kΩ/10kΩ rail voltage divider into the ESP32 ADC) must have a 1nF C0G bypass capacitor to GND placed at the divider junction (at R6.1 / VRAIL_DIV node). Value: 1nF C0G (Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D / LCSC C76947). fc ≈ 19kHz with the 47k||10k Thévenin source impedance.
rationale: The ESP32 SAR ADC requires charge from the S&H network at the ADC input. Without a capacitor at VRAIL_DIV, the ~38kΩ Thévenin source impedance limits charge delivery, causing ADC undersampling error. The 1nF C0G cap serves both the S&H charge reservoir and as an anti-alias filter (fc ≈ 19kHz matches the ~16.9kHz INA RC filter cutoff). C0G dielectric is required — X5R/X7R capacitance changes with bias voltage, adding gain error proportional to the measured rail voltage.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module only (modules/12vhpwr-standard). Identify: C24 on VRAIL_DIV net. Also applicable to any other board with a 47k/10k divider into an ESP32 ADC (24-pin if it has a divider).
check_method: Parse netlist for VRAIL_DIV net. Verify exactly one capacitor (C24) is present on this net to GND. Verify BOM value = 1nF, dielectric = C0G (from MPN or BOM note). Verify no X5R/X7R capacitor on VRAIL_DIV.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'VRAIL_DIV ADC cap DONE 2026-06-06 -- added C24 = 1nF C0G (Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D / C76947) VRAIL_DIV->GND, fc~19kHz with the 47k||10k source'; spec §6.1 12VHPWR Standard

title: REF3030 ratiometric reference bypass caps present
rule: The REF3030 (U4 on 12VHPWR Standard) must have both input and output bypass capacitors per the datasheet (typically 100nF on IN and 100nF on OUT, C0G or X7R, placed within 2mm of U4 pins). The REF3030 OUT must connect only to ESP32 ADC1 IO8 — not to any other load.
rationale: A voltage reference without bypass capacitors is susceptible to oscillation and noise coupling from adjacent switching regulators. The REF3030 is measured by the ADC for ratiometric correction — noise on its output directly adds measurement error. The spec explicitly adds bypass caps to the REF3030 BOM (CLAUDE.md v3.8 note: 'REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, cec-vendor:REF3030, MPN REF3030AIDBZR) + 2 bypass caps').
scope: 12VHPWR Standard module only. Identify: U4 with value REF3030 or REF3030AIDBZR. Check adjacent bypass caps on IN (pin 1) and OUT (pin 2) nets.
check_method: Parse netlist for U4 (REF3030). Verify at least one capacitor connects between U4 pin 1 (IN, net +3V3) and GND, and at least one capacitor connects between U4 pin 2 (OUT, net VREF) and GND. Verify VREF net connects to ESP32 ADC1 IO8 and no other load component (other than the ADC input and the bypass cap).
source: CLAUDE.md v3.8: 'REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, cec-vendor:REF3030, MPN REF3030AIDBZR) + 2 bypass caps'; spec §6.1: 'REF3030 OUT to ADC1 IO8 (freed by moving the SENSE0 sideband tap to IO15)'

title: TJA1051T/3 CAN transceiver bypass caps on VCC and VIO
rule: The TJA1051T/3 (U2 on all boards) must have: a 100nF bypass cap on VCC (pin 3, +3V3 or +5V per variant), a 100nF bypass cap on VIO (pin 5, +3V3), placed within 2mm of the respective pins. VCC and VIO must not share a single bypass cap.
rationale: The TJA1051T/3 datasheet requires separate decoupling on VCC and VIO. Without individual bypass caps, CAN transceiver switching transients couple onto the +3V3 rail and into adjacent signal lines. The CLAUDE.md 'decoupling brought up to the 24-pin gold standard' note specifically calls out 'dedicated TJA1051T/3 VCC/VIO bypass' as a requirement.
scope: All boards with TJA1051T/3 (U2 on all boards). Identify by: component value = 'TJA1051T/3' or 'TJA1051'. Check for bypass caps C_U2_VCC and C_U2_VIO (or by net: caps on +3V3 adjacent to U2).
check_method: Parse netlist for U2 (TJA1051). Find capacitors within 2mm of U2 (by BOM proximity or by net: caps on the +3V3 and VIO nets that also connect to U2 supply pins). Verify at least two caps are present (one per supply pin). Verify each is 100nF (value in BOM). Flag if missing or if VCC and VIO share one cap.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'dedicated TJA1051T/3 VCC/VIO bypass — the module U2 value is now TJA1051T/3 (C38695)'; spec §3.1 TJA1051T/3 locked; TJA1051T/3 datasheet decoupling requirement

title: M3 mounting holes GND-tied for chassis ground bond
rule: All M3 mounting holes (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via footprint) must be connected to the GND net via their copper pad. No M3 mounting hole may be isolated (no-connect or unconnected pad). The GND copper from the mounting pad must form a direct low-impedance path to the In1.Cu GND pour.
rationale: M3 screws into an aluminum chassis provide the low-impedance chassis ground bond that closes the EMC shield loop. An isolated mounting hole leaves the board floating relative to chassis, eliminating chassis-bond filtering and degrading radiated emissions. Spec §4: '4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via)'.
scope: All boards. Identify mounting holes: refs H1-H4 (or MK*) with footprint MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via. Verify each is on GND net.
check_method: Parse netlist for all mounting hole components (footprint contains 'MountingHole' and '3.2mm'). For each, verify pad 1 net is GND. Any mounting hole with an unconnected pad or explicit no-connect on its pad is a violation.
source: CLAUDE.md: '4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (PC-standard fastener; MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via)'; spec §4 Hub Standard table; spec §6.6 thermal design: 'Couple the high-current copper to the chassis through the mounting points'

title: SK6812 LED data line 3.3V→5V level shift buffer required
rule: The SK6812 LED data input line (DL1.DIN on Hub Standard) must be driven through the SN74AHCT1G08 (U6, configured as buffer with both inputs tied to LED_DATA GPIO) + 330Ω series resistor (R14) + 100nF bypass cap (C14 on U6 VCC). The ESP32 GPIO must NOT drive the LED data line directly at 3.3V.
rationale: The SK6812 V_IH threshold at 5V VDD is 0.7 × VDD = 3.5V. The ESP32 GPIO drives only 3.3V — below the guaranteed V_IH. Direct drive causes unreliable LED initialization and intermittent wrong color/behavior, especially on power-up. The AHCT buffer input uses TTL threshold (~2V), so 3.3V ESP GPIO reliably drives it, and the AHCT output is 5V-rail logic, reliably high for the SK6812. The 330Ω series resistor limits inrush to the first LED input capacitance.
scope: Hub Standard board only (the only board with SK6812 LEDs). Identify: DL1 (SK6812 chain, 7 LEDs). Check U6 = SN74AHCT1G08 (or equivalent AHCT AND gate configured as buffer). R14 = 330Ω between U6 output and DL1.DIN. C14 = 100nF on U6 VCC pin.
check_method: Parse netlist: verify U6 (value = SN74AHCT1G08 or 74AHCT1G08) exists with both input pins connected to the LED_DATA net. Verify U6 output connects to R14, and R14 output connects to DL1 (SK6812 first LED) DIN. Verify C14 (100nF) on U6 VCC between VCC and GND. Verify ESP32 GPIO (IO25) connects to U6 inputs, NOT directly to DL1.DIN.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'SK6812 data level shift (2026-06-05): the ESP32's 3.3 V GPIO is below the 5 V SK6812 V_IH (0.7*VDD ~= 3.5 V), so the LED data line is buffered up to 5 V by U6 (SN74AHCT1G08 single 2-input AND with both inputs tied = a non-inverting AHCT buffer; SOT-23-5, VCC=+5VSB, C14 100 nF) with R14 330 ohm series into DL1.DIN'; spec §4 Hub Standard table

title: NanoKVM aux UART lines: 33Ω series resistors + ESD clamp on KVM_3V3_REF
rule: On the Hub Standard J7 NanoKVM aux header: UART TX (J7 pin 3) and UART RX (J7 pin 4) must each have a 33Ω series resistor (R19 and R20) between the header pin and the ESP32 GPIO. The KVM_3V3_REF line (J7 pin 5) must have a PESD5V0S1BA ESD clamp (D7, cathode to KVM_3V3_REF, anode to GND).
rationale: The NanoKVM UART lines exit the board on a cable — any external cable is an antenna. The 33Ω series resistors damp reflections and limit inrush current if the NanoKVM's UART pin is driven before the Hub boots (collision protection). The PESD5V0S1BA on KVM_3V3_REF protects the ESP32 ADC1 IO1 pin from ESD on the cabled reference line (same rationale as the DETECT pin ESD diode — CLAUDE.md: 'D7 (PESD5V0S1BA, C5261083) ESD-clamps the cabled ref pin').
scope: Hub Standard only (hubs/hub-standard, J7 = S5B-PH-K-S 5-pin right-angle JST-PH). Identify: R19 (33Ω on J7.TX→ESP IO11), R20 (33Ω on J7.RX→ESP IO12), D7 (PESD5V0S1BA on J7.KVM_3V3_REF→GND).
check_method: Parse netlist: verify R19 and R20 (value ≈ 33Ω) on the UART_TX and UART_RX nets between J7 pins 3/4 and ESP32 IO11/IO12. Verify D7 (value = PESD5V0S1BA, footprint SOD-323) with cathode on KVM_3V3_REF net and anode on GND. Flag if any element is missing.
source: CLAUDE.md action item 0: 'UART TX -> 33ohm R19 -> ESP IO11, 4 = UART RX -> 33ohm R20 -> ESP IO12'; 'D7 (PESD5V0S1BA, C5261083) ESD-clamps the cabled ref pin'; spec §2.9 NanoKVM aux header

title: §6.13 detection comparator threshold RC: 10kΩ + 100nF PWM filter
rule: On EPS/PCIe Standard modules, the firmware-settable comparator threshold path must include: MCU PWM output (THRESH_PWM / IO14) → 10kΩ series resistor (R10) → 100nF shunt cap (C40) to GND → TLV7011 REF+ input. The RC filter fc = 1/(2π × 10kΩ × 100nF) ≈ 159Hz, smoothing the PWM to a stable DC threshold voltage.
rationale: Without the RC filter, the PWM signal drives the comparator reference directly, causing the comparator to toggle at the PWM frequency (typically tens of kHz) rather than triggering on actual load transients. This would produce thousands of false FREEZE triggers per second. The 159Hz filter cutoff is slow enough to present a stable DC reference while still allowing firmware to change the threshold setting in ~10ms.
scope: EPS 8-pin and PCIe 8-pin modules after §6.13 implementation (modules/eps-8pin, modules/pcie-8pin-2port, modules/pcie-8pin-3port). Identify: R10 (10kΩ) on THRESH_PWM net, C40 (100nF) between THRESH node and GND, feeding TLV7011 REF+ input.
check_method: Parse netlist: find R10 with one end on THRESH_PWM net and one end on THRESH node. Find C40 between THRESH node and GND. Find TLV7011 (U30-32) REF+ input connected to THRESH node. Verify value R10 = 10kΩ, C40 = 100nF. Flag if RC network is absent or if THRESH_PWM connects directly to comparator REF+ without filter.
source: CLAUDE.md: '§6.13 chain netlist-verified per cable (shunt SENSE_HI -> INA181A2 gain-50 -> TLV7011 comparator -> firmware THRESH (MCU PWM IO14 + R10 10k/C40 100n) -> per-cable DET -> MCU GPIO latch, ORs into FREEZE)'; spec §6.13

title: High-current via arrays must not block signal routing corridors
rule: On EPS and PCIe boards, the via arrays beneath each cable shunt (vertical transition for ~40-55A) must be contained within the cable column (the region directly under the J_IN/J_OUT connector pair and shunt). No via must be placed in the signal routing corridor (the central band between cable columns used for I2C, CAN, THRESH, DETECT spine routing).
rationale: CLAUDE.md action -2 explicitly requires 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as a deferred hard constraint for the synth placer. High-current vias in the signal spine force the router to detour CAN_H/CAN_L, I2C, and THRESH traces around via anti-pad voids, increasing trace length and potentially breaking the GND plane continuity check. The spec §6.7 'keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids' is the normative basis.
scope: EPS 8-pin and PCIe 8-pin modules. Identify cable columns: x-regions from J_IN to J_OUT pads. Identify signal corridor: x-region between the outermost cable column edges, toward the control/logic side of the board. Identify high-current vias: vias on nets containing '12V' or '/SENSEC' or on GND net within the cable column region.
check_method: Parse board for via positions on high-current nets. Compute the cable column bounding boxes (from J_IN/J_OUT pad centroids ±half the connector width). Verify all high-current vias are within cable column bounding boxes. Flag any high-current via in the signal corridor region between columns.
source: spec §6.7: 'Via arrays punch anti-pad voids in the L2 ground pour; keep signal traces and their returns clear of the voids'; CLAUDE.md action -2: 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as deferred hard constraint; cec_fr.add_power_pours() implementation

title: Hub Pro USB High Speed 90Ω ±5% differential impedance (advisory pending Pro spec)
rule: When Hub Pro is fully specified, USB_D_P/USB_D_N must be routed to 90Ω ±5% differential impedance for USB High Speed (480Mbps). Track width and gap must be calculated from the actual Hub Pro PCB stackup using a field solver or the JLCPCB impedance calculator. Skew between D+ and D− must be ≤5ps (inter-pair delay matching).
rationale: USB High Speed at 480Mbps requires 90Ω ±5% differential impedance (USB 2.0 specification). The Hub Standard uses Full Speed (12Mbps) where ±15% is tolerable — the hub-standard.kicad_dru comment explicitly notes 'FS is impedance-tolerant, so on THIS (Standard) board ~90ohm diff is good-practice-not-critical -- the strict 90ohm discipline matters on Hub Pro (USB High Speed, 480 Mbps)'. This constraint should be promoted to hard when Hub Pro PCB is laid out.
scope: Hub Pro only (hubs/hub-pro). Currently soft/advisory because Hub Pro is not yet fully specified. When Hub Pro PCB exists: apply impedance-controlled layer stackup, calculate W/S for 90Ω differential, set USB netclass in .kicad_pro to those dimensions, order impedance-controlled from JLCPCB.
check_method: When Hub Pro PCB exists: verify .kicad_pro USB netclass diff_pair_width and diff_pair_gap match the stackup-calculated 90Ω values (from JLCPCB impedance calculator for the specific prepreg/core stackup). Verify no USB HS track deviates >±5% from target width. Currently not checkable (board not yet laid out).
source: hubs/hub-standard/hub-standard.kicad_dru lines 36-47: 'the strict 90ohm discipline matters on Hub Pro (USB High Speed, 480 Mbps)'; spec §5 Hub Pro: 'USB High Speed'
